narrative:
The model has predicted a 23% chance that you will fail your final year, which is significant enough to require you to take remedial courses. This means that, based on various factors in your profile, the model suggests that additional support will be beneficial for your academic success.

The most influential factors in this prediction include your study habits, your past academic performance, and your aspirations for higher education. While you have not failed any classes before, which typically indicates a positive trend, your current study time is less than two hours a week. This is notably lower than many of your peers, where the majority study between two to five hours weekly. This lack of study time is pushing the prediction toward a higher risk of failing.

Additionally, while you have a strong desire to pursue higher education, which is a positive indicator, it does not outweigh the concerns raised by your study habits. The model also considers your family background, where both parents have completed only up to the 5th to 9th grade. This may suggest less academic support at home, which can impact your performance.

Given these insights, it is crucial for you to engage in remedial courses. These courses will provide you with the necessary support to improve your study habits and reinforce your understanding of the material. It’s also advisable to increase your study time and seek additional resources or tutoring to help you succeed in your final year.
